print: et E est B-triviale. (no exponent p)
note: The TeX silently corrects the print; the proof shows E is B^p-triviale ('Dire que E est B^p-triviale' a few lines above). Revised 5 Nov after a check of the mathematics: (21.2.1, (i)) gives an A-homomorphic section, i.e. A-triviality (18.2.3); the earlier correction B^p-triviale repeated the proof's hypothesis. By (0, 19.9.8.1) with Λ = B^p (discrete), 'B formally smooth over A relative to B^p' means: every commutative A-extension E of B by a B-module L that is B^p-trivial is A-trivial. The proof assumes E B^p-trivial ('Dire que E est B^p-triviale signifie ...'), uses the B^p-section v to get u(q(z)^p) = v(q(z))^p = z^p (L^p = 0 since L^2 = 0), i.e. the condition of (21.2.1, (i)) with 𝔎 = L; (21.2.1, (i)) then gives an A-homomorphism B → E right inverse to q, which is the definition (18.2.3) of an A-trivial extension. So the conclusion is 'A-triviale'. 'B^p-triviale' is the hypothesis (a circular conclusion that proves nothing), and 'B-triviale' has no meaning for an A-extension of B (A ⊂ B). Update MISPRINTS p. 158 ('correct') accordingly.

where: IV-4 p. 221, proof of (19.8.2) (i): F_s = F (x)_{O_X} k(s) and (F_lambda)_{s_lambda} = F_lambda (x)_{O_{X_lambda}} k(s_lambda)

correct: $\sh F_s=\sh F\otimes_{\sh O_S}\boldsymbol{k}(s)$ and $(\sh F_\lambda)_{s_\lambda}=\sh F_\lambda\otimes_{\sh O_{S_\lambda}}\boldsymbol{k}(s_\lambda)$
note: 𝓕_s is the module on the fibre X_s = X ×_S Spec k(s) whose sections f_i⊗1 are tested with (19.8.1, (i)) over the field k(s); by (I, 9.1.2) this is 𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝒌(s) = p*(𝓕) on X ×_S Spec k(s). The subscript must be the base: k(s) is an 𝒪_S-algebra through Spec k(s) → S, and Spec k(s) is not an X-prescheme, so ⊗_{𝒪_X} k(s) is undefined (the only residue fields that are 𝒪_X-algebras are the k(x), x ∈ X, and 𝓕⊗_{𝒪_X}k(x) is a k(x)-vector space, not a module on X_s). The same holds for X_λ → S_λ and s_λ. Elsewhere EGA writes the fibre module with the base subscript, 𝓕_y = 𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_Y} k(y) (e.g. EGA IV, §§11, 12, 15). A scan of the corrected French, English and Spanish texts (which follow the print here) finds the O_X form for a base point s only at this place and at IV-3 p. 54 and IV-4 p. 254 (entries below, both checked on the scan). Only the subscript changes; the argument is untouched.

The proof is the module statement: ψ'_R is ψ_A-semilinear and S generates (gr_•(R)⊗_A A/𝔍)[T_1..T_n] as a module over (gr_𝔎(A)⊗_A A/𝔍)[T_1..T_n], so Im(ψ'_R) = Σ ψ_A(c)ψ'_R(s) is the sub-ψ_A(...)-module generated by S', and ψ_A surjective makes it the sub-gr_𝔏(A)-module generated by S'; hence c) ⇔ c'). Card|σ| = h+1 for degree h in (0, 11.8.2)). So the term Tor_q(C^{-h}, C^{-k}) of degree (h, k) runs over Card(σ) = 1−h, Card(τ) = 1−k. print: On peut donc se borner au cas où K = k[T_1, ..., T_n]; alors K⊗_kL est un anneau de fractions de (square brackets; run_IVback/page_349_s4.png)

where: (Err_IV, 44), p. 358: 'dont toute partie fermée admet donc un seul point générique'
print: Y est un espace de Kolmogoroff localement noethérien, dont toute partie fermée admet donc un seul point générique (run_IVback/page_358_s1.png and _s2.png)
correct: dont toute partie fermée irréductible admet donc un seul point générique
note: A point y is a generic point of a closed set F when F is the closure of {y}; such an F is irreducible, so a reducible closed subset has no generic point and the printed sentence is false as it stands. What the Kolmogorov (T0) property gives ('donc') is uniqueness of the generic point of an irreducible closed subset, and that is what the paragraph uses: its first sentence ('toute partie fermée irréductible n'admet qu'un seul point générique') and its last ('toute partie fermée irréductible de X a un point générique unique') both say 'irréductible'. The word was dropped; the English and Spanish already have it.

where: IV-4 p. 324, proof of (21.14.1): 'tout idéal premier q de B non contenu dans p est principal'
print: Tout revient évidemment à prouver que tout idéal premier 𝔮 de B non contenu dans 𝔭 est principal. (run_IV4/page_324_s1.png)
correct: tout idéal premier $\mathfrak q$ de $B$ de hauteur $1$ non contenu dans $\mathfrak p$ est principal
note: A 1-codimensional cycle on Spec(B) is a combination of height-1 primes; if Z is principal at 𝔭, Z − div(f) involves only height-1 primes 𝔮 ⊄ 𝔭, so the theorem reduces to: every height-1 prime 𝔮 ⊄ 𝔭 is principal. The proof proves exactly that: it uses that 𝔮 is divisorial (𝔮D_0 divisorial by Bourbaki AC VII §1 no 10 prop 15) and that 𝔮_1 = 𝔮∩A[T] is a prime of height 1. Without the qualifier the claim is false: for A a complete DVR and B = A[[T]] (hypotheses hold, dim B = 2 > 1), the maximal ideal (π, T) is prime, not contained in 𝔭 = πB, and not principal. 'de hauteur 1' was dropped; the English ('of height one') and the Spanish ('de altura 1', with a footnote) already have it.
